reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED (no arguments) returns 21 alphanumeric characters: yyyymmdd, hh 00-23, mm, ss, hundredths, then '+', '-' or '0' and the offset hours and minutes from Greenwich Mean Time ('-' at most 12 h, '+' at most 13 h, '0' with 0000), denoting the local compilation time.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 window: refuses a function whose catalog IntroducedIn exceeds the dialect level; WHEN-COMPILED carries IntroducedIn 85 so it is admitted at 85 as at 2023

reader.edition-search: Read the stamp path end to end (catalog row -> binder -> ProgramEmitter Lazy capture -> IntrinsicRenderer WhenCompiled arm -> CobolDate.Format21); grepped WhenCompiled/WHEN-COMPILED/DialectLevel/Edition in those members: only the catalog window consults the edition; Format21 and the capture are edition-independent.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness pins length, digit ranges, sign/offset consistency and constancy; it does not pin a contained program's stamp (RV2) or reference modification of the value, which the probe wc1 covers. The '0' (no offset facility) arm is unreachable on .NET.

probes.expected: 21 characters per RV1 with local time behind GMT shown as '-0800'; group move and refmod of the value; contained program returns the same compilation stamp (RV2)

probes.printed: error COBOL1504: FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO §2023:15.3)
probes.expected: refused: the general format A.2.46.2 has no argument

probes.printed: LENGTH 21 / FIELDS Y / OFFSET Y / CLOCK ADVANCED Y / SAME STAMP Y / COMPILED NOT AFTER RUN Y (MATCH)
first version (wc1-001) refused PIC 9(21) (COBOL0802, 18-digit limit at 85) and FUNCTION LENGTH as a DISPLAY operand (COBOL0900, integer function as identifier requires 2002)
probes.expected: both are 1985 restrictions of other rules, correctly refused; WHEN-COMPILED itself is accepted at 85

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.46.3 RV1  (2.46.3 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1 [Two numeric digits of the hours past midnight, in the range 00 through 23]
OK  §1989:A.2.46.3 RV1  (2.46.3 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1 [two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13]
OK  §1989:A.2.46.3 RV2  (2.46.3 Returned Values)  the text is in RV2

reader.notes: The stamp is captured once per compilation from DateTimeOffset.Now and formatted by the one Format21 (yyyyMMddHHmmssff, sign, |offset hours|, |offset minutes|), baked as a constant; a fractional negative offset such as -03:30 renders -0330 by the Math.Abs arms. Edge left as a note, not a defect: a host at UTC+14 would yield '+14', outside RV1's 00-13, a zone the 1989 text predates; the only alternative ('0') would falsely claim no offset facility. The refusal diagnostic cites §2023 rather than the 1985 text (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: Read CobolDate.Format21 (yyyyMMddHHmmssff + sign by Offset>=0 + |Offset.Hours| + |Offset.Minutes|, InvariantCulture Gregorian) and ProgramEmitter's Lazy per-compilation capture via CompilationInputs.ReadCompilationTime; no listing carries a compile time (DATE-COMPILED is only a comment paragraph), so nothing can disagree with the stamp. Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-185/runs): rw1-001 WHEN-COMPILED as argument of REVERSE and NUMVAL(refmod 1:8), INSPECT TALLYING subject, STRING sender with POINTER, relation against CURRENT-DATE and a stored copy, refmod 17:1 / 18:4 / 9:2 -> '[2026111601345995-0800]', REV correct, NUMVAL 20261116, PTR 24 (21 chars), COMPILED BEFORE NOW, CONSTANT, SIGN OK, OFFSET NUMERIC, HOUR OK; rw2-001 'FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED ()' refused COBOL0900 (empty argument list is a 2002 form, general format A.2.46.2 has none); rw3-001 as a MOVE receiver refused COBOL5506 (A.2.3: functions cannot be receiving operands); rw4-001 in COMPUTE refused COBOL0844 (alphanumeric function, not arithmetic operand). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.46.3 RV1 [two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13]. Only unreachable edge: a UTC+14 host would emit '+14', outside RV1's 00-13, a zone for which RV1 has no conforming encoding; not probeable on this host (.NET on Windows ignores TZ) and not a code defect of this rule.
